_comment: TUI/GUI parity manifest (docs/workflows/tui-e2e-plan.md §7). The Flutter GUI has no Go test runner, so this checked-in manifest is the shared contract between internal/tui and ui/flutter_ui. When a surface changes legitimately, update BOTH the code and this manifest in the same commit. gui:false marks a TUI-only item; every deviation MUST have a justification in `deviations`. GUI sources of truth: ui/flutter_ui/lib/widgets/command_palette.dart (palette items), ui/flutter_ui/lib/core/shortcuts.dart (shortcuts), ui/flutter_ui status widgets (status bar).

deviations.palette:queue: no flutter queue route yet (documented deviation, command_palette.dart header comment)
deviations.palette:toggle sidebar: no flutter sidebar surface (documented deviation, command_palette.dart header comment)
deviations.shortcut:ctrl+m: markdown rendering toggle is TUI-only; the GUI renders markdown natively
deviations.shortcut:ctrl+d: pending-changes review modal is TUI-only today; GUI review lives in the diff panel
deviations.shortcut:ctrl+b: branches disabled by default in both surfaces; shortcut only bound when branches_enabled
deviations.shortcut:ctrl+c: GUI semantics differ: single press stops the active turn (sends /stop) instead of TUI double-press quit — the GUI has no quit concept
deviations.status:branch: CONDITIONAL both surfaces (session has a leaf message): TUI shows 'branch: <session name>'; GUI shows the active thread topic label via GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/threads/active (status_bar.dart sessionBranchProvider)
deviations.status:pending changes: CONDITIONAL both surfaces (>0): 'N pending changes' in warning color; TUI counts from the pending-changes registry, GUI via SdkApiClient.listPendingChanges (status_bar.dart sessionPendingChangesProvider)
deviations.status:claims to review: CONDITIONAL both surfaces (>0): 'N claims to review' in warning color; both fed by the memory.reviewQueue RPC — GUI via GET /api/v1/memory/review-queue (status_bar.dart memoryReviewPendingProvider)
deviations.status:connection dot: ● connection indicator renders as an ANSI dot; GUI shows a colored badge (same semantics, different glyph)
